skills.name: AI-assisted clinical documentation
skills.description: Use approved tools to draft structured notes while retaining clinical review and patient privacy.
skills.why: Cut the time you spend on notes while you stay the one who checks them.
skills.first_action: Map one de-identified patient-note workflow and list every required human check.

skills.name: High-stakes patient communication
skills.description: Explain uncertainty, options, and next steps in language a patient and family can act on.
skills.why: Patients still want a person to explain the options and decide with them.
skills.first_action: Practice a teach-back conversation for one common condition this week.

skills.name: Clinical informatics workflow design
skills.description: Improve how clinical data is captured, validated, handed over, and used in care decisions.
skills.why: Turns the software everyone complains about into something that improves care.
skills.first_action: Diagram one patient journey and mark duplicate data entry and safety risks.

skills.name: Precision agriculture operations
skills.description: Use field observations, sensors, satellite data, and simple decision rules to target farm inputs.
skills.why: Pairs what you know about your land with data that lifts yield and cuts waste.
skills.first_action: Choose one plot and record location, input, weather, and yield data for a full cycle.

skills.name: Farm-record analysis
skills.description: Turn input, labour, loss, sales, and yield records into practical farm decisions.
skills.why: Shows you where the money actually goes, and which jobs a tool could do for you.
skills.first_action: Record the cost and output of one product line in a simple weekly table.

skills.name: Climate-risk farm planning
skills.description: Use seasonal forecasts, water constraints, crop suitability, and contingency triggers in farm plans.
skills.why: Reading changing weather and adapting to it is not something software can do for you.
skills.first_action: Write three weather triggers and the action each should activate this season.

skills.name: AI-assisted reconciliation and exception review
skills.description: Use automation to match transactions, then investigate anomalies and document controls.
skills.why: Moves your day from matching numbers to deciding what to do about the odd ones.
skills.first_action: Classify last month’s reconciliation exceptions by cause and control owner.

skills.name: Technology-aware financial controls
skills.description: Design approvals, evidence trails, access controls, and reviews around automated finance workflows.
skills.why: The more that runs automatically, the more you are needed to catch when it goes wrong.
skills.first_action: Select one automated workflow and document its failure modes and compensating controls.

skills.name: Financial advisory communication
skills.description: Translate financial evidence into choices, trade-offs, and recommendations for a specific decision-maker.
skills.why: Clients pay for advice they trust, not for a report anything can produce.
skills.first_action: Rewrite one monthly report as three decisions, with evidence and consequences.

skills.name: Electronic vehicle diagnostics
skills.description: Use scan tools, wiring diagrams, live data, and fault trees to diagnose modern vehicle systems.
skills.why: Repair work is shifting from swapping parts to proving what the fault really is.
skills.first_action: Practice a documented fault-tree diagnosis on one common sensor code.

skills.name: Hybrid and EV safety servicing
skills.description: Safely isolate, inspect, and service high-voltage vehicle systems within local standards.
skills.why: A growing specialty that needs real hands, proper certification and someone accountable for safety.
skills.first_action: Identify an accredited high-voltage safety course and its entry requirements.

skills.name: Evidence-based repair communication
skills.description: Show customers what failed, explain options clearly, and document the agreed repair.
skills.why: Honest advice brings people back, and sets you apart from someone who just swaps parts.
skills.first_action: Create a photo-and-checklist handover for your next completed repair.

skills.name: AI-era creative direction
skills.description: Set a distinctive concept, reference system, audience intent, and quality bar before generating assets.
skills.why: When anyone can produce the work cheaply, knowing what is good becomes the job.
skills.first_action: Write a one-page creative rationale before opening any design or generation tool.

skills.name: Creative AI workflow orchestration
skills.description: Combine research, generation, editing, versioning, and human review into a repeatable creative workflow.
skills.why: The value is in running and checking the whole process, not in the output itself.
skills.first_action: Run one brief through a documented human–AI workflow and compare time, quality, and originality.

skills.name: Creative rights and provenance
skills.description: Manage licensing, consent, attribution, training-data concerns, and provenance for AI-assisted assets.
skills.why: Creative work you sell has to hold up legally, not just look good.
skills.first_action: Add source, rights, consent, and AI-use fields to your project handoff checklist.

skills.name: AI-supported lesson differentiation
skills.description: Adapt examples, scaffolds, and practice activities to learner needs while verifying curriculum alignment.
skills.why: Let AI do the prep so you keep your time for the students themselves.
skills.first_action: Create three difficulty levels for one lesson and test them with learner feedback.

skills.name: Student mentoring and early support
skills.description: Recognize learning or wellbeing barriers and coordinate appropriate support with students and caregivers.
skills.why: A student who trusts you will tell you things no system will ever pick up.
skills.first_action: Add a private two-question learner check-in to one class routine.

skills.name: Role-specific cybersecurity practice
skills.description: Protect accounts, devices, records, and workflows using controls appropriate to the role.
skills.why: Bringing in AI without security opens holes that land on you when they are found.
skills.first_action: Enable multi-factor authentication and inventory where work data is stored.

skills.name: AI output verification
skills.description: Check generated work against sources, constraints, calculations, and domain-specific failure modes.
skills.why: Anyone can get an answer from AI. Being the person who can tell if it is right is the valuable part.
skills.first_action: Create a five-item verification checklist for the AI task you use most.

skills.name: Workflow mapping and automation triage
skills.description: Separate repetitive steps from judgment, exceptions, relationships, and accountable decisions.
skills.why: Lets you hand off the dull work and keep the parts that need you.
skills.first_action: Map one weekly process and label each step automate, assist, or human-only.

skills.name: Customer discovery interviews
skills.description: Find unmet needs through structured conversations and turn evidence into a service decision.
skills.why: Talking to your own customers tells you more than any generic tool will.
skills.first_action: Interview five customers about the last time they struggled with the problem you solve.

skills.name: Small-business unit economics
skills.description: Track contribution margin, cash cycle, stock loss, and the true cost of serving one customer.
skills.why: Knowing what each sale really earns you makes pricing decisions obvious.
skills.first_action: Calculate revenue minus direct costs for one product or service unit.

skills.name: Local digital customer acquisition
skills.description: Use maps, messaging, social proof, and simple campaigns to reach nearby customers ethically.
skills.why: Brings in more customers without losing what makes a local business worth visiting.
skills.first_action: Create a complete business profile with hours, location, offer, and three proof points.

skills.name: Dynamic safety risk assessment
skills.description: Identify hazards, assess changing conditions, communicate controls, and stop unsafe work.
skills.why: When safety is on the line, someone has to be there and be responsible.
skills.first_action: Run a pre-task hazard review and document one changed condition before your next job.

skills.name: Consultative selling
skills.description: Diagnose the customer’s situation, shape a suitable option, and earn commitment without pressure.
skills.why: Big purchases are won on trust and good judgement, not a scripted pitch.
skills.first_action: Replace your opening pitch with three diagnostic questions in the next five conversations.

skills.name: Decision-focused data storytelling
skills.description: Turn analysis into a clear claim, evidence, uncertainty, and recommended decision.
skills.why: AI can make the chart. Saying what it means and standing behind it is the skill.
skills.first_action: Rebuild one report around a single decision and remove every chart that does not support it.

skills.name: Incident coordination under pressure
skills.description: Build shared situational awareness, assign decisions, communicate priorities, and adapt as evidence changes.
skills.why: When things go wrong, people follow someone they trust who can make the call.
skills.first_action: Run a 30-minute tabletop exercise for one plausible operational failure.

skills.name: AI governance in regulated work
skills.description: Decide where AI may assist, what evidence is required, who approves outputs, and how decisions are audited.
skills.why: Regulated employers need someone who knows both the rules and how the AI actually works.
skills.first_action: Write an acceptable-use boundary for one AI-assisted task in your profession.

skills.name: Service blueprinting
skills.description: Map a customer journey, frontstage interactions, backstage work, evidence, delays, and failure points.
skills.why: Makes the service better and shows you which steps are safe to automate.
skills.first_action: Map one real customer journey from request to follow-up and mark its worst handoff.

skills.name: Technical systems thinking
skills.description: Trace dependencies, failure modes, trade-offs, and downstream consequences before changing a system.
skills.why: AI writes code fast, which makes deciding how it should be built worth more.
skills.first_action: Draw a dependency and failure map for one system you maintain.

skills.name: Digital source verification
skills.description: Verify origin, context, manipulation, and corroboration before publishing or acting on digital material.
skills.why: The more fakes there are, the more people pay for someone who can check.
skills.first_action: Build a source-check protocol and apply it to one high-risk claim.

skills.name: Coaching and developmental feedback
skills.description: Observe performance, diagnose the barrier, and agree a practical next step with another person.
skills.why: People improve through someone who knows them, not through generic advice.
skills.first_action: Use situation–behavior–impact feedback in one conversation this week.

skills.name: Evidence-based project estimation
skills.description: Estimate effort, material, uncertainty, and contingency using comparable work and explicit assumptions.
skills.why: Giving a date you can actually hit is what separates you from a guess.
skills.first_action: For the next job, record estimate assumptions and compare them with actual time and material.
